_comment: Where the palm beach belongs: the coast of a warm or hot Age, from the shallows up the foot of the climb
(notes/palm-beach-design.md). Read by BiomeHome, which widens only temperature and humidity as the
biome is asked for more strongly -- where it stands on the ground stays put.
Continentalness is Grounding's height curve: -2..+8 over the waterline reads as -0.15, -10 as -0.3,
+20 as -0.04. So -0.27 is about eight under (the lagoon's edge) and -0.11 about twelve over, part-way
up an island's shoulder. Erosion is the sandy side of vanilla's -0.2225 line.
Temperature is vanilla's temperate, warm and hot bands, from -0.15. It began at 0.2, warm only, and an
ordinary Age that named it plainly got none (measured 2026-09-30, scripts/checks/palm-beach.txt): its
coasts read temperate, and a page that does nothing is the silent drop. From temperate, an ordinary Age's
coast is palm beach where it is mild and vanilla beach where it is cool, a cold Age wants a stronger
naming, and a frozen one practically never has it -- the risk the writer takes.
Two depths, as vanilla gives every surface biome: the surface itself and the ground under it.
